title: Learning English
cando: say what you can do, ask for help in class and write a short note

about.text: In this lesson you are in an English class. You ask for help. You say what you can do and what you like doing. You read a course timetable and write a short note. Then you enrol on a course.
goals: Ask for help in class: Can you say that again? What does … mean?
Say what you can and can't do: I can swim. I can't drive.
Say what you like doing: I like cooking. I love dancing.
Read a course timetable. Write a short note with capital letters and full stops.
Enrol on a course: ask about the days, the times and the level.

chapters.title: In class
chapters.text:
In this lesson you are in an English class.
The teacher speaks, and Mei doesn't understand. That's OK. She asks for help.
She says: Sorry, can you say that again, please?
She asks about a new word: What does free time mean?
And she asks: How do you spell dancing?
Asking is good. It helps you learn.

chapters.title: can, and like with -ing
chapters.text:
To say what you can do, use can and a verb. I can swim. I can dance.
The verb after can has no to and no s. She can drive.
For no, say can't. I can't drive.
Listen: can is short and quiet, and can't is long and strong.
To say what you like doing, use like and a verb with -ing. I like cooking. I love dancing.

chapters.title: A timetable and a note
chapters.text:
Next, you read a course timetable. Look for the days, the times, the rooms and the levels.
Then you write a short note to your teacher.
Start every sentence with a capital letter. End it with a full stop or a question mark.
Names and days have capital letters too: Monday, Ms Clarke.

chapters.title: Enrolling on a course
chapters.text:
Then you enrol on an English course.
Say: I'd like to enrol on an English course, please.
Ask about the days, the times and the level.
Say what you can do. I can read a little, but I can't write well.
You don't understand? Say: Can you say that again, please?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about learning something new.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You don't understand a word in class. What do you do?
choices: ask the person next to me
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. All three are good. Asking is never a problem: teachers want your questions.

conversation.title: In class
conversation.setting: It is Monday evening. Mei is at her English class after work.
lines: Good evening. Please open your books at page 12.
Sorry, can you say that again, please?
Of course. Page 12. Today's topic is free time.
It means time with no work. You can do what you like.
So, Mei, what can you do in your free time?
I can swim, and I can dance. I love dancing.
No, I can't. I go to work by bus.
Now write three sentences about you, with can and like.
D-A-N-C-I-N-G. Remember: dance, but dancing has no e.
OK. I can remember that. Thanks.

questions.q: What is the topic of the lesson?
questions.why: The teacher says: Today's topic is free time.
Mei says: I can swim, and I can dance.

questions.q: How does Mei go to work?
questions.why: Mei says: No, I can't. I go to work by bus.

phrases.text: Sorry, can you say that again, please?
phrases.use: When you did not hear or did not understand.
Asking for the letters of a word.
A short answer to Can you …?
Saying what you like doing very much.

items.meaning: One more time.
items.example: Can you say that again, please?

items.meaning: To say something one more time.
items.example: Can you repeat the question, please?

items.meaning: To say or show an idea. A word or a sign does this.
items.example: What does this word mean?

items.meaning: To know what something says or how it works.
items.example: Sorry, I don't understand.

items.meaning: A group of letters with its own idea, like book or pen.
items.example: I write new words in my notebook.

items.meaning: Something you ask. When you write it, it ends with this mark: ?
items.example: Can I ask a question?

items.meaning: The words that people speak and write, like English or Arabic.

items.meaning: The language of Britain, the USA and many other countries.
items.example: My English is better every week.

items.meaning: To say words, or to use a language.

items.meaning: To look at words and understand them.
items.example: I read the news on my phone.

sound.title: can or can't
sound.explain: In a sentence, can is short and quiet: I can swim. Can't is long and strong: I can't swim. The t is very quiet, so listen for the long, strong sound. In a short answer, can is strong too: Yes, I can. Listen, then say each group.
groups: I can swim · I can't swim
She can drive · She can't drive
Yes, I can · No, I can't
lines: I can swim, and I can dance.

sayIt.instructions: Say Mei's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Is your can short, and your can't long?
lines: Sorry, can you say that again, please?
I can swim, and I can dance. I love dancing.
No, I can't. I go to work by bus.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Three use can. One says what Mei likes doing.
examples: I can swim, and I can dance.
spot.question: What comes after can: swim or swimming? Where does can go in the question? What comes after love?
spot.answer: After can, the verb has no -ing and no to: I can swim. In a question, can goes first: Can you drive? The short answer is No, I can't. After love and like, use a verb with -ing: I love dancing.

rules.title: can and can't
rule: can + a verb: I can swim. She can drive.
can't = cannot: I can't sing. He can't drive.
Question: Can you speak Arabic? Yes, I can. No, I can't.
The same for everyone: I can, he can, they can. No s.
rules.mistake: Not: I can to swim. Not: She cans drive. Say: I can swim. She can drive.

rules.title: like + -ing: I like cooking
rule: like, love, don't like, hate + a verb with -ing: I like cooking.
An e at the end goes: dance → dancing, drive → driving.
Some verbs get two letters: swim → swimming, run → running.
Question: Do you like reading? Yes, I do. No, I don't.
rules.mistake: Not: I like cook. Say: I like cooking.

practice.q: I ___ swim, but I can't dance.
practice.why: But joins a yes and a no: I can swim, but I can't dance.
After can, the verb has no s and no -ing.

practice.q: ___ you speak French? Yes, I can.
practice.why: The answer has can, so the question starts with can.
The question has can, so the answer has can't.
like + a verb with -ing: I like cooking.

practice.q: My brother loves ___ . He goes to the pool every day.
Do you like ___ ? Yes, I dance every Friday.
I don't like ___ . I take the bus to work.
practice.why: don't like + a verb with -ing: driving.
Say that again means say it one more time.
After does, the verb has no s: What does it mean?

yourTurn.prompt: Write four sentences about you. Say two things you can do and one thing you can't do. Then say what you like doing.
yourTurn.model: I can cook, and I can speak two languages. I can't swim. I like reading, but I don't like running.

text.title: English courses at Northfield Adult College
text.body:
PRACTICE TIMETABLE: this college does not exist

NORTHFIELD ADULT COLLEGE
ENGLISH COURSES: SPRING

LEVEL 1 (beginners)
Monday and Wednesday, 6 pm to 8 pm, Room 4

LEVEL 2
Tuesday and Thursday, 6 pm to 8 pm, Room 4

SPEAKING CLUB (all levels)
Saturday, 10 am to 12 pm, Room 11

The courses start on Monday 7 April.
There are no lessons in the week of 26 May.

Please bring a notebook and a pen to every lesson.
You can borrow a dictionary from the library.
Homework: one page every week.

To enrol, come to the office in Room 1.
The office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm.

What must you bring to every lesson?

model.title: A note to my teacher
model.body:
Hello Ms Clarke,
I'm sorry, but I can't come to the lesson on Wednesday.
I start work at five on Wednesdays this month.
Can I come to the speaking club on Saturday?
My homework is in the box in Room 4.
Thank you,
Priya Shah

write.task: Write a short note to your teacher, like the model. Say you can't come to one lesson and say why. Then ask one question. Write four or five sentences.
checklist: Every sentence starts with a capital letter.
Names, days and I have capital letters: Ms Clarke, Monday, I.
Every sentence ends with a full stop or a question mark.
I wrote my name at the end.

card.title: Enrol on a course
card.situation: You want to study English at Northfield Adult College. You go to the office. You work in the day, so evenings are best for you.
card.goal: Ask about the days, the times and the level. Say what you can already do in English.

phrases: I'd like to enrol on an English course, please.
What time does the course start?
Which level is good for me?
I can read a little, but I can't write well.
Sorry, can you say that again, please?
prepare.notes: Write what you can and can't do in English: speak, read, write, understand. Then write your best days and times.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher works in the college office. Ask about the days, the times and the levels. Say what you can already do. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You work in the office of an English college. I want to enrol on a course. Tell me the days and times of the courses. Ask me what I can do in English, and help me choose a level. Use simple English.

model.title: At the college office
lines: Yes, please. I'd like to enrol on an English course.
Of course. What can you do in English?
I can speak a little, and I can read short texts.
Not very well. I can't write long sentences.
Then Level 1 is good for you.
Monday and Wednesday, from six to eight.
Sorry, can you say that again, please?
Monday and Wednesday, six to eight in the evening.
Great. I finish work at five, so that's fine.
Good. Please fill in this form.
compare: Did you say: I'd like to enrol on an English course?
Did you ask about the days and the times?
Did you say what you can and can't do in English?
Did you ask the person to say it again when you did not understand?

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Who is learning? What are they learning, do you think?
reading.talk: What is easy for you in English? What is difficult? Write three sentences with can and can't, or tell Wehel.

quiz.q: I ___ swim, so I don't go to the pool.
quiz.why: I don't go to the pool, so it is a no: can't.

quiz.q: Can you speak Arabic? Yes, I ___ .
quiz.why: The question has can, so the answer has can.

quiz.q: She likes ___ . She makes dinner every day.

quiz.why: The letters of a word answer How do you spell …?

quiz.q: Look at the ___ . The lesson is at six on Monday.
quiz.why: A timetable shows the days and times.

quiz.q: Every sentence ends with a ___ or a question mark.
quiz.why: A full stop is the small dot at the end of a sentence.

quiz.q: Sorry, I don't understand. Can you ___ that, please?
quiz.why: Repeat means say it one more time.

quiz.q: There ___ three rooms in my flat.
quiz.why: Three rooms is more than one, so there are.

quiz.q: Ana has a sister. ___ name is Marta.
quiz.why: The sister is a woman, so her.
Your brother is he, so does.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the class conversation in pairs. Each learner asks: Can you say that again? What does … mean? How do you spell …?
Day 2: find someone who can swim, can drive or likes cooking. Learners ask Can you …? and Do you like …ing?, then tell the class.
Day 3: the college office. You are the office assistant. Each learner enrols on a course, asks about the days, times and level, and says what they can do; then change roles.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their notes to the teacher aloud.
